Playbook.name: Forcepoint DLP — Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public Email - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Forcepoint DLP flagged bulk sensitive data sent to personal/public email (gmail/outlook/yahoo etc.). Triage: exfiltration to personal email, or a legitimate business exception?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Sending sensitive data to personal email is a classic exfiltration and insider-threat vector.

Assets.AssetType: Forcepoint DLP endpoints and web/email gateways

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Forcepoint DLP CEF (verified live). Fields: cef.extensions.loginName (user), cef.extensions.sourceHost, cef.extensions.sourceIp, cef.extensions.destinationHosts (destination URL/host), cef.extensions.deviceAction (Permitted/Blocked), cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory (data type), cef.extensions.severityType, cef.extensions.sourceServiceName (channel: Content Gateway/Email).

Signal.Name: Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public
Signal.Details: Forcepoint DLP Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public Email.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the Forcepoint DLP transfer is data exfiltration or legitimate business data handling.

Step.name: Confirm the DLP transfer: user, data, destination, action
Step.Purpose: Identify who moved what to where, and whether it was Permitted (completed) or Blocked.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.sourceServiceName RLIKE "(?i).*(email|content gateway).*" AND cef.extensions.destinationHosts RLIKE "(?i).*(gmail|outlook|yahoo|hotmail|proton).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, cef.extensions.loginName, cef.extensions.sourceHost, cef.extensions.destinationHosts, cef.extensions.deviceAction, cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory, cef.extensions.severityType | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Sensitive files to a personal email domain, Permitted, is exfil. Note the data category and volume. A one-off small permitted item may be an incidental business exception; a bulk transfer is exfil.

Step.name: Volume/pattern for this user
Step.Purpose: A burst of sensitive transfers by one user indicates exfil vs a single incidental transfer.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.loginName == "$user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS transfers = COUNT(*), permitted = COUNT(CASE(cef.extensions.deviceAction RLIKE "(?i).*permit.*", 1, null)), destinations = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.destinationHosts) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many permitted sensitive transfers to varied external destinations = exfil. One blocked transfer = policy working.

Node.Condition: Bulk sensitive data Permitted to a personal/public email domain.
Node.Result: True Positive (Exfiltration to Personal Email - escalate, compliance)

Node.Condition: A legitimate business transfer to an approved destination, or a blocked attempt (policy working).
A DLP policy over-classifying benign data.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FP-TRANSFER, INV-02-FP-VOLUME to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate, approved transfer or a blocked attempt.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm business justification; close as benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: Exfiltration of sensitive data to personal email.

SOCAction.Item: Involve DLP/compliance; review the data; interview the user; reset the account if compromised; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A DLP policy over-classifying benign data.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the user (loginName), the data and the destination.
If exfil, involve DLP/compliance and review the transfer.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Review the transferred data with DLP/compliance; interview the user; reset the account if compromised.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Tune DLP policies; enforce egress controls; educate users; block risky destinations.

QualityChecks.Check: Forcepoint deviceAction Permitted vs Blocked distinguishes a completed transfer from a blocked one; loginName is the user.
severityType HIGH is the reshaped rule's focus.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Exfil scoped with compliance; user addressed; account secured.
